aims: Correctness, not operating characteristics: every deterministic output equals a known answer, and R equals Python
dgm: Hand-built fixtures (pathology zoo, key E) plus property-based generators of random designs: nesting/crossing with label reuse, mobility, aliased factors, empty cells, NA tokens, Unicode/whitespace level variants, factor orders, singleton clusters, rank-deficient X
estimands: Exact outputs: counts, level sets, ID maps, ranks, identifiability verdicts, ceilings, d_g budgets, LP separation verdicts
methods: R implementation vs Python implementation vs brute-force reference (SVD rank on small designs; two LP solvers for separation)
performance: Agreement rate (target 100%); count of 'near threshold' statuses; generated-case counts
reps: Property tests: >= 10,000 random designs per property per nightly CI run; fixtures: all
mcse_target: Not applicable (deterministic); any disagreement outside declared tolerance is a bug
cost: Seconds to minutes in CI; L1-01/L7-01 implicit-nesting vs mobility classifier gets a small fit-free Monte Carlo (label-reuse rate {0,.5,1} x mobility rate {0,.02,.1}; 10,000 reps per cell; laptop)

checks: All Gaussian Stream A flags (L4-01..06, L4-08, L4-10..11, L5-01..05, L5-08..13, L5-18..20, L6-12, L7-11) and Stream B predictions run on the same replicates; family-level multiplicity (L5-15)
aims: (a) false-flag rate (FFR) of every check under a correctly specified model; (b) number of flags per report and P(>= 1 consequential flag); (c) baseline focal performance (Type I error, coverage) for later comparison
dgm: V1a nested 2-level: J {6,10,20,40,100} x m {2,5,20,50} x cluster-size CV {0,.5} x ICC {.1,.3} x slope SD {0,.15,.3} (240 cells). V1b crossed 1-factor Latin square: (S,I) {(12,8),(24,16),(48,32),(96,64)} x slope SD {0,.1,.3} (12). V1c crossed 2x2 within: (24,16),(48,32) x slope SD {0,.2} (4). V1d 3-level/CRT: schools {4,10,20,40} x classes {2,4} x pupils {10,25} x randomisation level {class, school} (32). V1e growth: persons {50,200,800} x waves {3,5,8} x time-slope SD {0,.3} (18). Residual SD 1; fixed effects for a level-1, a level-2 and a cross-level term
estimands: Flag (0/1) and statistic of each check; focal: beta of level-1, level-2 and cross-level terms, variance components
methods: Suite check (R; Python where implemented) vs engine-native flag (lme4 messages, glmmTMB pdHess) vs pinned comparators in default configuration (performance::check_*, DHARMa tests where applicable) vs naive variant named in the catalogue item; oracle (true model) where defined
performance: FFR per check x cell; distribution of flag counts per report; P(>=1 consequential flag); Type I error and coverage of focal tests (Satterthwaite; KR on cells with n <= 400); failure and non-convergence rates
mcse_target: FFR and Type I error at .05: MCSE .0049; coverage at .95: .0049; family-wise rate at .10: .0067
decision_rule: A check is 'calibrated' in a cell if the upper 95% Monte Carlo limit of its FFR is <= 1.5 x nominal for test-based checks (<= .075 at alpha .05) and <= .05 for descriptive flags graded 'consequential'. Report-level: P(>=1 consequential flag) <= .10 per cell, otherwise gate or downgrade checks (L5-15). Cells outside these limits are written to the registry as 'not calibrated in region'
cost: Central 125 CPU-h (V1a 47, V1b 25, V1c 34, V1d 5, V1e 14); range 75-250

checks: Gaussian post-fit checks against their targeted misspecification: M01 level-1 heteroscedasticity (L5-03, L5-10); M02 skewed or heavy-tailed random effects (L5-04); M03 skewed or heavy-tailed residuals (L5-01); M04 AR(1) residuals in growth data (L5-11, L7-11); M05 omitted contextual effect (L5-12, L7-07); M06 omitted random slope (L1-17, Heisig & Schaeffer); M07 outlying clusters (L5-08, L5-09); M08 omitted curvature (L5-02); M09 level-2 heteroscedasticity by arm (L5-10, L7-04); M10 omitted randomisation level in a CRT (L7-03); M11 informative cluster size (L7-13); M12 ceiling/floor censoring (L3-12, L7-20); M13 dyads with negative dependence (L7-08, negligible cost)
aims: (a) detection rate (DR) by magnitude; (b) consequence: impact of each misspecification on focal estimands, unconditionally and conditional on flag status; (c) cross-talk: flag rates of every other check under each module (specificity matrix feeding the dependency graph); (d) action value: focal performance of 'switch to the registry alternative when flagged' vs 'never switch' vs 'always use the alternative' (Shamsudheen & Hennig 2023)
dgm: Each module at 3 magnitudes, applied to 8 representative cells of V1: nested (J,m) in {(10,5),(10,20),(40,5),(40,20)} with slope SD .15, crossed (24,16) and (48,32), 3-level (10 schools, 4 classes, 10 pupils), growth (200 persons, 5 waves); about 3/4 of module x cell pairs are applicable (216 cells). Middle magnitude set in the pilot to the smallest value that makes a focal estimand fail the harm criterion; preregistered after the pilot
estimands: Flag of the targeted check and of all other checks; focal beta (bias, coverage, Type I error) under the fitted model and under the registry alternative
methods: Suite check (R; Python where implemented) vs engine-native flag (lme4 messages, glmmTMB pdHess) vs pinned comparators in default configuration (performance::check_*, DHARMa tests where applicable) vs naive variant named in the catalogue item; oracle (true model) where defined; registry alternative model per module (e.g., glmmTMB dispformula, AR(1), cluster-mean centring, censored model)
performance: DR by magnitude with MCSE; ROC/AUC of continuous statistics; harm = coverage < .925, Type I error > .075 or |relative bias| > 10% for a focal estimand; miss rate given harm; conditional coverage and bias by flag status; action-value contrasts
reps: 1,000 per module x magnitude x cell; influence module adds 200 replicates with full cluster-deletion refits
mcse_target: DR worst case MCSE .0158; bias MCSE .032 x EmpSE; conditional measures only if >= 200 replicates in the conditioning set
decision_rule: Assessability field: 'adequate' if DR >= .80 at the smallest harmful magnitude, 'weak' if .50-.80, 'not assessable' if < .50 in that region. Consequence field 'consequential' only where harm is shown at magnitudes the check detects with DR >= .50. Thresholds may be retuned only on a calibration half of the replicates and must be confirmed on the held-out half; tuned values carry the study ID as provenance

checks: L4-01..L4-06, L4-08, L4-21, L5-20 (singularity criterion, convergence triage, boundary probe, gating of degenerate downstream checks); sibling key B's H3
aims: Agreement of the suite's unit-free singularity criterion and convergence taxonomy with a reference optimum; scale invariance; engine dependence of flags
dgm: Nested J {6,10,20} x m {5,20} x true slope SD {0,.05,.1,.2} x predictor scaling {x/10, x, 10x} (72 cells); crossed 1-factor and 2x2 at (24,16),(48,32) x slope SD {0,.05,.2} (12 cells)
estimands: Rank of the true and estimated RE covariance; whether the reported optimum equals the best objective over 7 optimisers and restarts (allFit-style reference); flag of each criterion
methods: Suite criterion vs lme4 isSingular (tol 1e-4) vs glmmTMB pdHess/NA SEs vs statsmodels boundary warning vs reference optimum
performance: Sensitivity/specificity of singularity flags against the true rank; triage error rates (warning on a true optimum; silence on a false optimum); invariance of verdicts to scaling (agreement rate across the 3 scalings)
reps: 1,000 per nested cell; 500 per crossed cell
decision_rule: Criterion adopted if scale invariance is 100% (by construction) and its specificity and sensitivity are each >= lme4's in every cell (upper and lower 95% MC limits); otherwise report both

checks: L4-12, L4-13, L4-15 (boundary tests, parametric bootstrap LRT, CIs for variance components)
aims: Type I error and power of the 50:50 chi-bar-square, exact RLRT (RLRsim, comparator) and parametric bootstrap LRT with few clusters; coverage of profile vs Wald CIs for variance components
dgm: Nested J {5,10,20} x m {5,20} x slope variance {0,.05,.15} (18 cells)
estimands: Rejection of H0: slope variance = 0; CI coverage for variance components
methods: chi-bar-square, RLRT, PB-LRT (B = 199; Boos & Zhang 2000 extrapolation as a check on the B needed), Wald and profile CIs
performance: Type I error, power, coverage, refit-failure rate in bootstrap samples
mcse_target: Type I error .0069; power worst case .0158
decision_rule: Default test is the one with Type I error within [.025,.075] in all cells and highest power; PB used where chi-bar-square fails

checks: L1-17 reduction ladder and stopping rules (sibling key B: H1 stopping rules, H2 ordering, H5 few-cluster education designs, H7 post-selection reporting, H9 masked execution)
aims: Operating characteristics of each stopping rule on the same pre-specified ladder: Type I error, power, coverage, rung distribution
dgm: As in key B's hpc_simulation_plan.tsv (H1: 200 Latin-hypercube cells over subjects {12..96} x items {8..64} x slope SD {0..0.8} x correlation x MCAR missingness x coding). Recommended change: cap 2x2 maximal cells at 1,536 rows (48 x 32), because the uncapped grid costs 2.2 times more
methods: Stopping rules listed in key B
performance: Type I error, power, coverage, bias/RMSE, rung distribution, convergence and singular rates, runtime
decision_rule: Key B's rules; rules with Type I error upper MC limit > .075 in any cell are not offered as defaults
cost: Central 703 CPU-h with the cap (H1 662, H2+H5 41); 1,473 uncapped. Key B's own estimate for H1 (200 CPU-h) assumed 0.07 s per fit; measured 2x2 maximal fits take 0.7 s (384 rows) to 4.1 s (1,536 rows) and an extrapolated 23 s (6,144 rows)

checks: L1-05, L1-08, L1-18, L1-21 (pre-fit predictions: confounding verdicts, precision and boundary probabilities, outcome-blind design analysis, forecasts of fit-time behaviour); key B's H6
aims: Calibration of the predicted probabilities the suite reports before fitting
dgm: 20 design cells (14 nested, 6 crossed) x assumed-vs-true variance mismatch {exact, 0.5x, 2x}
estimands: Predicted P(singular fit), P(rung reached), predicted SE of variance components vs realised
methods: Suite's design analysis (inner simulations from assumed variances) vs realised fits
performance: Brier score, reliability curves, calibration slope/intercept
decision_rule: Messages show predicted probabilities only where calibration slope is within [0.8, 1.25]; elsewhere 'not assessable'

checks: L4-19, L4-20, L6-03, L6-05, L6-10, L6-12 (cross-language and cross-engine parity on generated data)
aims: Agreement of flags and summaries between R and Python and between engines; rate of 'near threshold' disagreements
dgm: Subsets of V1: nested (12 cells) and small crossed (2 cells; statsmodels crossed variance-component fits grow about quadratically: 0.95 s at 1,536 rows, 16.7 s at 6,144 rows)
methods: lme4 vs glmmTMB vs statsmodels (plus any promoted engine from key A)
performance: Agreement rate; disagreements classified as expected (registry) or unexpected
decision_rule: Unexpected disagreement > 0 blocks the parity claim for that output
cost: About 1 CPU-h (Python), R side reused from V1

checks: GLMM checks under a correct model: L3-04 (Hauck-Donner screen), L3-05..09 (residuals, dispersion, OLRE, zero inflation), L3-17/L4-17 (Laplace accuracy), L5-06, L5-07, L5-13, L5-22
aims: FFR of each GLMM check; baseline focal performance; Laplace vs AGQ discrepancy where AGQ is available
dgm: Families {Bernoulli, binomial with 5 trials, Poisson} x nested J {10,20,40,100} x m {5,20,50} x latent ICC {.1,.3} x slope SD {0,.3} (48 cells per family) plus crossed (24,16),(48,32) x slope SD {0,.3} (4 per family)
methods: Suite check (R; Python where implemented) vs engine-native flag (lme4 messages, glmmTMB pdHess) vs pinned comparators in default configuration (performance::check_*, DHARMa tests where applicable) vs naive variant named in the catalogue item; oracle (true model) where defined; DHARMa simulate-without-refit residuals as comparator
decision_rule: As V1. Bernoulli dispersion checks must be reported as 'not assessable', never 'pass' (L3-07)

checks: GLMM misspecification modules: G01 overdispersion (OLRE or NB), G02 zero inflation, G03 quasi-separation and rare events, G04 non-normal random effects, G05 omitted random slope, G06 Laplace inaccuracy (small m, large RE variance)
dgm: Each module at 3 magnitudes x 6 cells
methods: As V2 with glmmTMB alternatives (nbinom2, ziformula, OLRE) and nAGQ where available

checks: L4-12, L4-13 for GLMMs (boundary tests and PB-LRT)
dgm: Nested J {10,20} x m {5,20} x slope variance {0,.3} (6 cells)
performance: Type I error, power, refit failures
mcse_target: Type I error .0097; power worst case .0224
